svg.title: A V100 node, from DRAM to CUDA cores
svg.desc: One node with a CPU socket and DDR4 DRAM, a PCIe switch, an InfiniBand or Ethernet NIC, and two Tesla V100 GPUs joined by NVLink. Each GPU has a PCIe host interface, 80 SMs with 5120 FP32 CUDA cores and 640 tensor cores, a 6 MB L2 cache, eight memory controllers, and four HBM2 stacks giving around 900 GB/s. One SM is shown with its four partitions. Four numbered paths show local HBM2 math, the halo exchange over NVLink, host copies over PCIe, and off node traffic through the NIC, next to the peak bandwidth of each link.
svg.text: A V100 node, from DRAM to CUDA cores
The further data sits from the SMs the slower it moves, and the CPU path is ~9x slower than NVLink.
Gen3 x16 per GPU, ~16 GB/s each way
